device.category: electromechanical desktop synthesizer: eight motor oscillators in two voices plus a digital voice, 4-note polyphony, analogue filters
device.based_on: Successor to the MOTOR Synth (MKI), the first electromechanical polysynth (Riga, Latvia); MKII adds the DCO voice, expanded portamento, detune and cross-mod controls.

architecture.polyphony_mode: 4 notes: each MOTOR VOICE has four motors (poly, duo or unison per voice) and the DCO four digital oscillators; up to 3 voices per note. Polyphonic before the filters, paraphonic after.
architecture.patch_memory_note: Presets and projects (with sequencer patterns, arp patterns and motion recordings) on internal memory and microSD.
architecture.summary: Each MOTOR VOICE is four custom brushless DC motors. Spinning speed sets pitch; each motor's sound is read either electromagnetically (the 'M' wave from a pickup beside the rotating coils, akin to a tonewheel organ) or optically (infrared sensors reading sine, saw and square patterns printed on reflective discs, with deliberate imperfections). Physical inertia slews every pitch change; ACCEL and BRAKE extend that into a pitch envelope (or portamento). Each motor has its own amp envelope and VCA; the four are mixed, sent through a pre-filter send/return, drive and an analogue multimode filter (LP24, BP12, HP12, AP24, self-oscillating) per voice. A DCO voice (four digital oscillators with six waves, PWM, folding, sync) runs alongside with a digital twin filter. Cross mod (FM or ring), drift/detune, three assignable modulators with envelopes, arpeggiator, 8-pattern sequencer, motion recording, audio input processing.
architecture.synthesis_note: Electromechanical: pitch is motor rotation speed; waveforms are physical readouts (electromagnetic induction and optical disc reflection), not electronic oscillators.

modules.name: Performance interface and voice allocation
modules.description: 8-key non-velocity keypad with scales and microtuning, four PITCH ENCODERS (per-voice detune, momentary pitchwheel), MIDI, CV/trigger, arpeggiator and sequencer; per-voice poly/duo/unison and performance-tool assignment.

modules.name: MOTOR VOICE 1 motor drive and inertia (ACCEL / BRAKE)
modules.description: Converts note pitch to target motor speed. Inertia gives an inherent rev-up/rev-down slew; ACCEL (on note-on, from the FROM interval) and BRAKE (on note-off, to the TO interval) extend it as a pitch envelope, or act as rise/fall portamento in GLIDE mode. Per motor (polyphonic).

modules.name: MOTOR VOICE 1 motors
modules.description: Four brushless DC motors per voice (soft-mounted, acoustically treated). Outputs per motor: M (electromagnetic inductive pickup), OPT SINE, OPT SAW, OPT SQ (infrared reading of reflective disc patterns). Imperfect readout is part of the character.

modules.name: MOTOR VOICE 1 WAVE selector
modules.description: Chooses which motor readout feeds the voice.

modules.name: MOTOR VOICE 1 analogue tone tilt
modules.description: Tilt EQ before the mix: follows SCALE (low boost at low scales, high boost at high) or manual.

modules.name: MOTOR VOICE 1 amp envelope
modules.description: Per-motor envelope: ADSR, AD, AR, DADSR, ADSHR, AD loop or ADS with curve.

modules.name: MOTOR VOICE 1 motor VCAs
modules.description: One analogue VCA per motor, under its amp envelope; VOLUME sets the peak.

modules.name: MOTOR VOICE 1 motor mix
modules.description: Mixes the voice's four motors (paraphonic from here on); DCO can be routed in.

modules.name: MOTOR VOICE 1 drive
modules.description: Analogue drive circuit before the filter (0 unity to 100 maximum distortion).

modules.name: MOTOR VOICE 1 analogue filter
modules.description: Analogue multimode filter: LP24, BP12, HP12, AP24; resonance self-oscillates (~87); calibrated key tracking with glide.

modules.name: MOTOR VOICE 1 filter envelope
modules.description: Filter envelope (same modes as the amp envelopes) to cutoff by ENV AMOUNT.

modules.name: MOTOR VOICE 2 motor drive and inertia (ACCEL / BRAKE)
modules.description: Converts note pitch to target motor speed. modules.description: Four virtual-analogue oscillators (paraphonic or unison): six waveshapes including noise, PWM, wave folding, hard sync; own amp and pitch envelopes.

modules.name: DCO amp envelope
modules.description: Amp envelope for the DCO oscillators.

modules.name: DCO VCAs
modules.description: One per digital oscillator.

modules.name: DCO filter envelope
modules.description: Filter envelope for the DCO's digital filter.

modules.name: DCO digital filter
modules.description: Digital emulation of the analogue filter (same modes and parameters); the DCO can instead pass through either analogue filter.

modules.name: Cross mod
modules.description: Amplitude (RING) or frequency (FM) cross modulation between the two motor voices; from frenzied ring-mod distortion to a pulsating 'broken' sound.

modules.name: Drift / detune
modules.description: Gradual variation in motor rotation speeds: drift or static detune between motors, assignable per voice.

modules.name: Modulator 1
modules.description: Shapes STEP (up, down, noise, pattern, random), TRI, SQ, SAW UP, SAW DOWN with curve, PW, X/Y offset, slope; 0-32760 Hz; clock INT, another modulator, BPM or note; own mod envelope on depth; two destination slots.

modules.name: Modulator 2
modules.description: Shapes STEP (up, down, noise, pattern, random), TRI, SQ, SAW UP, SAW DOWN with curve, PW, X/Y offset, slope; 0-32760 Hz; clock INT, another modulator, BPM or note; own mod envelope on depth; two destination slots.

modules.name: Audio input processing
modules.description: External audio for filtering, gating, side-chaining and vocoder-style processing through the voices.

modules.name: Arpeggiator, sequencer and motion rec
modules.description: Arpeggiator with rhythm editor; 8 patterns per project with ratchets, micro-timing, probability; 8 motion-recording lanes; master tempo.

modules.name: Output
modules.description: Main out (TS mono, or TRS split V1/V2), headphones; MASTER VOLUME not stored.

behaviours.name: Motor oscillators
behaviours.rule: Each note sets a motor's rotation speed. The M wave comes from an electromagnetic pickup beside the coils (harmonically rich, responds well to drive); OPT SINE/SAW/SQ are infrared readings of printed patterns on a reflective disc, deliberately imperfect. Mechanical noise is damped by soft mounts and acoustic treatment.

behaviours.name: Inertia and ACCEL / BRAKE
behaviours.rule: Motors cannot change speed instantly, so every pitch change slews slightly. TARGET mode: each note starts FROM ±12 semitones away and reaches pitch at the ACCEL rate; on release it moves TO ±12 semitones at the BRAKE rate (curve -2 to +2). GLIDE mode: ACCEL sets rising, BRAKE falling portamento. Per motor; short gates may leave notes off-pitch (a usable detune).

behaviours.name: Polyphony and paraphony
behaviours.rule: Each voice's four motors can be poly (four notes), duo or unison; each motor has its own amp envelope and VCA. The four are then mixed into one analogue filter per voice (paraphonic), so filter key tracking follows the last note (with optional glide). The DCO mirrors this with four digital oscillators.

behaviours.name: Filters
behaviours.rule: Shared controls edit V1, V2 and DCO filters individually or linked: LP24, BP12, HP12, AP24, resonance to self-oscillation (~87), pre-filter drive, bipolar envelope amount, key tracking. Self-oscillating filters track pitch and can be played as oscillators.

behaviours.name: Cross mod and drift
behaviours.rule: CROSS MOD multiplies (RING) or frequency-modulates (FM) between the motor voices. DRIFT/DETUNE varies motor speeds for analogue-style detune or drift, assignable per voice.

behaviours.name: Modulators
behaviours.rule: Three modulators, each with two destinations (any parameter, including each other), independent depth and scale, a mod envelope on depth, five shapes with detailed shaping, and clocks from internal rate, another modulator, master tempo or note frequency (audio-rate possible).

behaviours.name: Performance
behaviours.rule: 8-key keypad with scales and microtuning, four pitch encoders, CLUTCH buffer, arpeggiator with rhythm editor, sequencer (8 patterns per project, chaining, ratchets, micro-timing, probability), 8 motion-rec lanes, randomiser; MIDI (incl. poly aftertouch controllers) and 3 CV / 3 trigger inputs.

not_in_source: DCO waveshape names and the exact DCO parameter ranges
source_inconsistencies: The CC map labels CC 77 'V1 ACCEL FROM' and CC 79 'V1 BRAKE TO' in the V2 block (they duplicate CC 73 and 75); they are taken as V2 FROM and V2 TO.
The Motor Controls chapter calls the optical saw both 'Optical Saw' and 'Optical Triangle "OPT SAW"'.
Retailer specifications list the all-pass filter as 12 dB; the manual says 24 dB all-pass.
Overview says amp envelope modes include ADSHR and AD Loop for amp and filter envelopes, while mod envelopes list five modes (no AD Loop, ADS).
Retailer copy describes cross mod as 'amplitude cross-modulation with either Voice 1 or Voice 2'; the MKI manual describes RING and FM modes with Voice 2 modulating.

modelling_gaps.detail: Uses the electromechanical_oscillator module type (schema 0.13.0); motor inertia is modelled as a slew limiter ahead of each motor, as the manual describes.
Several chapters came from search excerpts; DCO details, input processing routing and the matrix destination list are summarised.
Motor, envelope and VCA modules are per_voice (one per motor/note); mixers, filters and effects are per motor voice.
